Liraglutide significantly reduced the incidence of this primary composite outcome by 13% compared with placebo (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.78–0.97) [5][6][9]. This reduction was primarily driven by a significantly lower rate of cardiovascular death, which fell by 22% (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.66–0.93) [1][5]. The MACE benefit was consistent across subgroups based on sex, age, and baseline cardiovascular risk level [2]. In pooled analyses of SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6, semaglutide significantly reduced primary MACE (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.62–0.92, p = 0.0062) and expanded MACE (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68–0.95, p = 0.0097), with the effect independent of baseline cardiovascular risk except in people with prior heart failure [1][4][9].

answer: GLP-1 receptor agonists are thought to reduce cardiovascular events primarily through indirect mechanisms, including weight loss, blood pressure reduction, improved glycemic control, and anti-inflammatory effects [1]. Meta-regression data indicate that both systolic blood pressure and weight reductions are independently associated with MACE risk reduction, with blood pressure showing a stronger relationship in trials using ambulatory monitoring [5]. Proposed direct mechanisms include improved myocardial perfusion via endothelial modulation, antifibrotic effects on myocardium, reduced epicardial adipose tissue, autonomic modulation toward parasympathetic activity, and promotion of natriuresis and diuresis [1]. Additional direct effects comprise platelet inhibition, augmented fibrinolytic responses, and attenuated thrombogenesis [6], as well as improved endothelial function, reduced oxidative stress, and inhibition of myocardial cell apoptosis [7]. It remains unclear precisely how these treatments produce their cardiovascular effects, and further studies are required [9].

answer: The cardiovascular benefits of GLP-1 RAs and SGLT2 inhibitors appear to be complementary rather than equivalent, with SGLT2 inhibitors primarily reducing the risk of heart failure hospitalisation, whereas GLP-1 RAs mainly reduce the risk of stroke and myocardial infarction [7]. Consistent with this, a real-world cohort found a significantly lower rate of heart failure admissions in the SGLT2i group (6.0% vs 10.6%), with SGLT2 inhibitors demonstrating a slightly superior overall cardiovascular profile [8], and a separate study reported marginally superior protection against MACE with SGLT2 inhibitors [4]. However, it remains unclear whether SGLT2 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists provide superior cardiovascular protection, as prior meta-analyses have yielded conflicting results [6], and head-to-head comparisons remain scarce [4]. The mechanisms proposed for these benefits overlap and include reduced insulin resistance, improved glucose and blood pressure control, weight reduction, reduced inflammation, and improved endothelial function [5], while their distinct mechanisms may be synergistic when combined [1][7].

In a nationwide Danish cohort of new users without prior stroke, GLP-1 RA use was associated with a significantly lower stroke risk compared with DPP-4 inhibitors [1][6], and a meta-analysis of GLP-1 RA cardiovascular outcome trials found a reduction in fatal or non-fatal stroke risk [8]. However, the effect is not uniform across all populations: in a meta-analysis of patients with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease, GLP-1 RAs reduced all-cause mortality and MACE but had no significant effect on stroke [7].

Some sources characterize GLP-1 RAs as primarily reducing atherosclerotic cardiovascular events rather than heart failure outcomes [2], and in heart transplant recipients GLP-1 RA use was not associated with hospitalization due to graft dysfunction (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.45–2.01) [4]. answer: The safety profile of GLP-1 RAs regarding pancreatitis is mixed: large cardiovascular outcome trials and meta-analyses have not demonstrated a statistically significant increase in acute pancreatitis risk compared with placebo, and no significant increase in acute pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer has been reported [1][4][9]. However, a large retrospective cohort study found that GLP-1 RA use was associated with a small increased risk of acute pancreatitis (HR 1.058, 95% CI 1.015–1.103), with the excess risk more pronounced during the first 6 months of treatment, while no differences were observed for chronic pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer [5][10]. Preclinical studies and pharmacovigilance reports have suggested a possible association with pancreatic diseases, though these risks remain unconfirmed as clinical trials were not powered to assess pancreatic safety [3]. Additionally, emerging case reports indicate that structural pancreatic abnormalities, including mucinous cystic lesions, may develop independently of pancreatitis [2]. Pancreatitis remains a warning on product labeling, and these agents should be used with caution in patients with a history of pancreatitis [9].

In a heart-failure meta-analysis, EXSCEL was the only included trial with more heart-failure events in the active arm, and its removal rendered the pooled heart-failure difference significant [3][7]. answer: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist rather than a selective GLP-1 receptor agonist, combining a GLP-1–based backbone with balanced agonism at GLP-1R and a fivefold higher affinity for GIPR [1][2]. Concurrent GIPR stimulation amplifies insulin release via PI3K–AKT signalling and, in vitro, produces supra-additive β-cell cAMP generation and insulin secretion compared with GLP-1 or GIP alone [2][10]. This dual mechanism additionally enhances insulin sensitivity, augments adiponectin-mediated lipid oxidation, and amplifies weight loss beyond that typically achieved with GLP-1 monotherapy [1][2][8]. Consequently, tirzepatide achieves greater reductions in body weight, visceral and ectopic fat (including pericardial/epicardial adipose tissue), and left-ventricular mass than selective GLP-1 receptor agonists [1]. Its single-molecule architecture was engineered by modifying the native GIP amino acid sequence to bind and activate both receptors, with a C20 fatty acid acylation extending its half-life to approximately 116 h [4].
